land.text: central and southern Anhui, formerly Qin's Jiujiang

predecessors.note: The Ying Bu page names no territory for Xiang Yu's Jiujiang; the Eighteen Kingdoms table gives 'central and southern Anhui'.

land.text: Jiujiang, where Long Ju 'defeated Ying Bu' and Xiang Yu's side regained the land

successors.note: Ying Bu fled to Liu Bang, who made him King of Huainan in 203 (Ying Bu page); Huainan is a separate kingdom (no Cliopatria row) and Cliopatria's Western Chu shape of 203 contains the Jiujiang outline.

capitals.name: Liu (Lu'an, Anhui)
capitals.note: Chinese Wikipedia, 英布: Xiang Yu '便立英布為九江王，以六為都' (Liu, present-day Lu'an, Anhui; the English Ying Bu page gives the same seat). Coordinates are Luan's in places.jsonl; inside the Cliopatria Jiujiang shape (reviewer, 2026-10-19).

rulers.name: Ying Bu (Qing Bu)
rulers.note: Infobox 'King of Jiujiang' tenure '207 - c.August 203 BC' covers Jiujiang and the later Huainan; the Jiujiang reign here stops when Long Ju takes the land.

keyframe_review.note: 86,995 km2 for 206-204, bbox 115.3-119.4 E, 29.9-33.1 N: the table's 'central and southern Anhui'. No page gives an area, so no infobox figure to compare. The Ying Bu and Long Ju pages put Long Ju's defeat of Ying Bu after 'late 205 BC' ('Months later'), so the land passes to Western Chu in 205-204, within the row's last year; the year of the handover is uncertain by up to a year (see ledger).

region.text: central and southern Anhui (Eighteen Kingdoms table), Ying Bu's Jiujiang

ledger.note: 206: Xiang Yu makes Ying Bu, his former general, King of Jiujiang. 'Xiang Yu later occupied Xianyang and divided the former Qin Empire into the Eighteen Kingdoms'; 'Ying Bu was named King of Jiujiang (九江王)'; 'In the fourth lunar month of 206 BC, the rulers of the Eighteen Kingdoms returned to their respective domains.' The Eighteen Kingdoms table: 'central and southern Anhui'.

region.text: central and southern Anhui (Eighteen Kingdoms table), Ying Bu's Jiujiang

ledger.note: Late 205: Xiang Yu sends Long Ju against Ying Bu. 'In late 205 BC, after Ying Bu betrayed Xiang Yu and defected to Liu Bang's side, Xiang Yu sent Long Ju to attack Ying Bu.' (The Chu-Han Contention page: 'In November 205 BCE, Ying Bu agreed to join Liu Bang and rebelled against Xiang Yu.')

region.text: central and southern Anhui (Eighteen Kingdoms table), Ying Bu's Jiujiang

ledger.note: 204: Long Ju defeats Ying Bu in Jiujiang. 'Long Ju defeated Ying Bu in Jiujiang and destroyed most of his forces' and Ying Bu 'had no choice but to flee ... and take shelter under Liu Bang'; the Ying Bu page says 'Months later Long Ju defeated Ying Bu and conquered Jiujiang'. Neither page dates the defeat; 204 is the researcher's year from 'late 205' plus 'months later', and it could be late 205.

region.text: central and southern Anhui (Eighteen Kingdoms table), Ying Bu's Jiujiang

ledger.note: 204: Jiujiang falls to Xiang Yu's side. 'Months later Long Ju defeated Ying Bu and conquered Jiujiang.' Page silent on the year; in 203 Liu Bang 'instated Ying Bu as King of Huainan' (a separate kingdom).

region.text: central and southern Anhui (Eighteen Kingdoms table), Ying Bu's Jiujiang

ledger.note: 204: the Kingdom of Jiujiang ends with Long Ju's conquest. Year as for the loss; Ying Bu rebelled again and was killed in 196 BC as Liu Bang's King of Huainan (Ying Bu page).

wars.name: Chu-Han Contention

zones.text: Jiujiang, where Long Ju defeated Ying Bu

wars.outcome: Han victory (infobox '206-202 BCE'). Jiujiang's king defected to Liu Bang in late 205, was beaten by Long Ju and fled; Xiang Yu's side took the land.
wars.note: Long Ju died in 204 (Wei River), so the conquest of Jiujiang precedes it. The Chu-Han page's 'unable to resist Long Ju's attacks, so he abandoned his domain in Jiujiang and joined Liu Bang' is undated.

certainty.note: The kingdom was assigned by Xiang Yu from commanderies; no survey or treaty lines; the outline is Cliopatria's approximation.

notes:
Wikidata Q5349053 is the Eighteen Kingdoms item shared by twelve Cliopatria rows; Jiujiang is its own kingdom (Ying Bu), so it keeps its own dossier.
Year of the fall: the pages agree only on the order (defection late 205, then Long Ju's attack, then flight to Liu Bang) and not on a year; 204 is chosen because Cliopatria's row ends then and 'months later' follows 'late 205'. If the defeat fell in the last weeks of 205, 204 belongs to Western Chu; the confidence-1 events flag this. The western-chu dossier (ea-02-a) has the matching gain in 203 'page silent', so western-chu needs a gain from jiujiang dated 204/205.
Ying Bu's later Kingdom of Huainan (203-196 BC; commanderies Jiujiang, Lushan, Hengshan and Yuzhang under him, per the Ying Bu page) is not in Cliopatria and needs a dossier from the additions batch. The capital Liu is the page's for Huainan; the Jiujiang seat itself is not on a page opened.
